We are about to study Raphael, the most generally praised, the most beautiful, and certainly the most loved of all the painters of the world. When all these delightful things can be truthfully said of one man, surely we may look forward with pleasure to a detailed study of his life and works.

arxiv-2012-06407.title: Hard gluon evolution in the last stage of the bottom-up thermalization
arxiv-2012-06407.creator: F. G. Ben, M. V. T. Machado
arxiv-2012-06407.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by F. G. Ben, M. V. T. Machado. The study of how fast thermalization in heavy ion collisions occurs has been one of the central topics in the heavy ion community. In the weak coupling picture this thermalization occurs from “the bottom up”: high energy partons, formed early in the collision, radiate low energy gluons which then proceed to equilibrate among themselves, forming a thermal bath that brings the high energy sector to equilibrium.

arxiv-2101-03939.title: Extremize Optical Chiralities through Polarization Singularities
arxiv-2101-03939.creator: Weijin Chen, Qingdong Yang, Yuntian Chen, Wei Liu
arxiv-2101-03939.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Weijin Chen, Qingdong Yang, Yuntian Chen, Wei Liu. Chiral optical effects are generally quantified along some specific incident directions of exciting waves (especially for extrinsic chiralities of achiral structures) or defined as direction-independent properties by averaging the responses among all structure orientations. Though of great significance for various applications, chirality extremization (maximized or minimized) with respect to incident directions or structure orientations have not been explored, especially in a systematic manner.

arxiv-2105-08329.title: Non volatile photo-switch using a diamond pn junction
arxiv-2105-08329.creator: Cédric Masante, Martin Kah, Clément Hébert, Nicolas Rouger, Julien Pernot
arxiv-2105-08329.description: Abstract Ultrawide bandgap semiconductor technologies offer potentially revolutionary advances in the rapidly developing areas of quantum communication, short wavelength optics, smart energy conversion and biomedical interfaces. These strongly demanding technologies can be partly constructed using conventional devices but new hybrid architectures are needed to overpass current performances and add functionalities.

arxiv-2109-01483.title: A Survey of the Proof-Theoretic Foundations of Logic Programming
arxiv-2109-01483.creator: Dale Miller Inria-Saclay & LIX, Ecole Polytechnique, Palaiseau, France
arxiv-2109-01483.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Dale Miller Inria-Saclay & LIX, Ecole Polytechnique, Palaiseau, France. Several formal systems, such as resolution and minimal model semantics, provide a framework for logic programming. In this paper, we will survey the use of structural proof theory as an alternative foundation. Researchers have been using this foundation for the past 35 years to elevate logic programming from its roots in first-order classical logic into higher-order versions of intuitionistic and linear logic.

arxiv-2301-03238.title: MAQA: A Multimodal QA Benchmark for Negation
arxiv-2301-03238.creator: Judith Yue Li, Aren Jansen, Qingqing Huang, Joonseok Lee, Ravi Ganti, Dima Kuzmin
arxiv-2301-03238.description: Abstract Multimodal learning can benefit from the representation power of pretrained Large Language Models (LLMs). However, state-of-the-art transformer based LLMs often ignore negations in natural language and there is no existing benchmark to quantitatively evaluate whether multimodal transformers inherit this weakness.

arxiv-2404-01951.title: Near-unity indistinguishability of single photons emitted from dissimilar and independent atomic quantum nodes
arxiv-2404-01951.creator: Félix Hoffet, Jan Lowinski, Lukas Heller, Auxiliadora Padrón-Brito, Hugues de Riedmatten
arxiv-2404-01951.description: Abstract Generating indistinguishable photons from independent nodes is an important challenge for the development of quantum networks. In this work, we demonstrate the generation of highly indistinguishable single photons from two dissimilar atomic quantum nodes. One node is based on a fully blockaded cold Rydberg ensemble and generates on-demand single photons.

arxiv-2412-10747.title: Optimal control of a kinetic equation Thanks: Department of Mathematical Sciences, University of Bath, Claverton Down, Bath BA2 7AY, UK. A.R.Pim@bath.ac.uk, tmp38@bath.ac.uk, amt83@bath.ac.uk
arxiv-2412-10747.creator: Aaron Pim, Tristan Pryer, Alex Trenam
arxiv-2412-10747.description: Abstract . This work addresses an optimal control problem constrained by a degenerate kinetic equation of parabolic-hyperbolic type. Using a hypocoercivity framework we establish the well-posedness of the problem and demonstrate that the optimal solutions exhibit a hypocoercive decay property, ensuring stability and robustness.

arxiv-2412-15461.title: Asymptotic Extinction in Large Coordination Games
arxiv-2412-15461.creator: Desmond Chan, Bart de Keijzer, Tobias Galla, Stefanos Leonardos, Carmine Ventre
arxiv-2412-15461.description: Abstract We study the exploration-exploitation trade-off for large multiplayer coordination games where players strategise via Q-Learning, a common learning framework in multi-agent reinforcement learning. Q-Learning is known to have two shortcomings, namely non-convergence and potential equilibrium selection problems, when there are multiple fixed points, called Quantal Response Equilibria (QRE).

arxiv-2501-11833.title: Is your LLM trapped in a Mental Set? Investigative study on how mental sets affect the reasoning capabilities of LLMs
arxiv-2501-11833.creator: Saiful Haq, Niyati Chhaya, Piyush Pandey, Pushpak Bhattacharya, IIT Bombay, Hyperbots Inc saifulhaq@cse.iitb.ac.in
arxiv-2501-11833.description: Abstract In this paper, we present an investigative study on how Mental Sets influence the reasoning capabilities of LLMs. LLMs have excelled in diverse natural language processing (NLP) tasks, driven by advancements in parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) and emergent capabilities like in-context learning (ICL).

arxiv-2509-00365.title: CRouting: Reducing Expensive Distance Calls in Graph-Based Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search
arxiv-2509-00365.creator: Zhenxin Li, Shuibing He, Jiahao Guo, Xuechen Zhang, Xian-He Sun, Gang Chen
arxiv-2509-00365.description: Abstract . Approximate nearest neighbor search (ANNS) is a crucial problem in information retrieval and AI applications. Recently, there has been a surge of interest in graph-based ANNS algorithms due to their superior efficiency and accuracy. However, the repeated computation of distances in high-dimensional spaces constitutes the primary time cost of graph-based methods.
